comments.author: CodersAcademy006
comments.body: Confirmed: in `_precompile_worker` (`torch/_inductor/runtime/triton_heuristics.py`, ~L756-764) the per-config compile loop only catches `(OutOfResources, PTXASError, IntelGPUError)` at L759, so a config whose generated Triton is structurally invalid raises `triton.compiler.errors.CompilationError`, which propagates out and aborts the whole precompile. During a normal `torch.compile` run this never surfaces because a working config is selected and the bad one is only compiled lazily; on cold AOT import every config is compiled up front, so the first invalid one crashes the load. Adding `CompilationError` to the caught tuple (it isn't currently imported in this file, so it needs the import too) would let it fall through to the existing "no valid configs" handling at L761, which already raises cleanly only when *all* configs fail. @XAheli

issues.title: torch.compile: InternalTorchDynamoError ('method' object has no attribute '__dict__') when tracing inspect.getfullargspec on a bound method
issues.author: bhimrazy
issues.body:
## 🐛 Describe the bug

Calling `inspect.getfullargspec()` on a bound method inside a compiled region raises an `InternalTorchDynamoError` on PyTorch 2.12 and 2.13. The same code works on 2.11 and earlier, where Dynamo graph-breaks on `inspect` and runs it eagerly.

The trigger needs the bound method to have been wrapped by Dynamo and then unwrapped again via `__wrapped__` before it's passed to `getfullargspec` — i.e. `obj.meth = compiled.dynamo_ctx(obj.meth)`, then `meth.__wrapped__`. This isn't contrived; it's what PyTorch Lightning does when a compiled model logs a metric (see the last section).

Minimal, self-contained reproducer (no third-party deps):

```python
import inspect
import torch


def takes_param(fn, name):
    if hasattr(fn, "__wrapped__"):
        fn = fn.__wrapped__          # dynamo ctx -> original bound method
    return name in inspect.getfullargspec(fn).args


class Model(torch.nn.Module):
    def step(self, x):
        takes_param(self.step, "dataloader_iter")   # introspect a bound method mid-trace
        return x * 2

    def forward(self, x):
        return self.step(x)


model = Model()
compiled = torch.compile(model)
model.step = compiled.dynamo_ctx(model.step)   # rebind step as a dynamo-wrapped method

compiled(torch.randn(4))
```

This is a tracing-stage failure, so it's independent of the backend — it reproduces with the default backend and never reaches a compiled graph.

I traced it into `torch/_dynamo/variables/dicts.py`. When Dynamo emulates the `obj.__signature__` lookup that `inspect._signature_from_callable` performs, it reaches `SideEffectsProxyDict.get_example_value_dict`, which does `object.__getattribute__(value, "__dict__")`. `method` objects have no `__dict__`, so this raises a raw `AttributeError` that escapes as `InternalTorchDynamoError` instead of either graph-breaking or being surfaced as an in-graph `AttributeError` that the `try/except` in `_signature_from_callable` would catch.

Possibly related but distinct: #147201 — same function, but that was an `Unsupported: 'skip function getfullargspec'` graph-break on a plain function and is closed as non-reproducible. This is a hard `InternalTorchDynamoError` on a **bound method**, new in 2.12.

## Error logs

```
  File ".../torch/_dynamo/variables/dicts.py", line 1430, in get_example_value_dict
    return object.__getattribute__(value, "__dict__")
torch._dynamo.exc.InternalTorchDynamoError: AttributeError: 'method' object has no attribute '__dict__'

from user code:
   File "repro.py", line 15, in forward
     return self.step(x)
   File "repro.py", line 11, in step
     takes_param(self.step, "dataloader_iter")
   File "repro.py", line 7, in takes_param
     return name in inspect.getfullargspec(fn).args
   File ".../inspect.py", line 1391, in getfullargspec
     sig = _signature_from_callable(func, ...)
   File ".../inspect.py", line 2547, in _signature_from_callable
     sig = obj.__signature__
```

## Versions

Observed across versions:

| torch  | result                                        |
| ------ | --------------------------------------------- |
| 2.11.0 | works (graph-breaks on `inspect`, runs eager) |
| 2.12.0 | `InternalTorchDynamoError`                     |
| 2.13.0 | `InternalTorchDynamoError`                     |

I reproduced the error locally on 2.13.0; the 2.12 failure was observed in CI, and 2.11 and earlier are unaffected (the same code path has been green there).

Environment where I reproduced it (from `collect_env.py`):

```
PyTorch version: 2.13.0
Is CUDA available: False
Python version: 3.12.12
OS: macOS-26.3-arm64-arm-64bit
```

## Where this shows up in practice

PyTorch Lightning hits this whenever a `torch.compile`d model calls `self.log()` during training. It rebinds the step methods to Dynamo-wrapped versions in [`compile.py`](https://github.com/Lightning-AI/pytorch-lightning/blob/master/src/lightning/pytorch/utilities/compile.py) and then introspects the step signature inside `self.log()` via [`is_param_in_hook_signature`](https://github.com/Lightning-AI/pytorch-lightning/blob/master/src/lightning/pytorch/utilities/signature_utils.py) — the `__wrapped__` + `getfullargspec` sequence above. Downstream tracking issue: https://github.com/Lightning-AI/pytorch-lightning/issues/21836.

---

> _Disclosure per the repo's [AI policy](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/main/AI_POLICY.md): I used Claude Code to help investigate and draft this report. I reproduced the failure locally on 2.13.0, saw the 2.12 failure in CI, and reviewed the root-cause pointer into `dicts.py` myself._

issues.title: [Inductor] AssertionError: len(index) == len(stride) in ir.py when using torch.compile(mode="max-autotune") on CPU BMM/GEMM
issues.author: xyt66665000
issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

When compiling an attention-like function containing complex numbers (`torch.polar`, `torch.view_as_complex`) and batched matrix multiplication (`torch.matmul`) on CPU with `torch.compile(mode="max-autotune")`, the compiler crashes with an `AssertionError`. 

The crash occurs during the C++ backend's BMM/GEMM template generation (`cpp_bmm_template.py`), specifically in the `indexer` function inside `torch/_inductor/ir.py` where it asserts `len(index) == len(stride)`.

A similar CUDA variant of this reproducer fails differently with KeyError: 'complex64' in Triton codegen.
I filed that separately because the failing backend path is different.

### Reproduction Script
```python
import torch

def target_function(
    l_tok_embeddings_weight_, l_tokens_, l_attn_norm_0_weight_, 
    l_wq_0_weight_, l_wk_0_weight_, l_wv_0_weight_, l_wo_0_weight_
):
    arange = torch.arange(0, 8, 2, device='cpu', dtype=torch.float32)
    angles = torch.true_divide(arange, 8)
    pow_1 = torch.pow(10000.0, angles)
    freqs = torch.true_divide(1.0, pow_1)
    t = torch.arange(0, 4, device='cpu', dtype=torch.float32)
    outer = torch.outer(t, freqs)
    freqs_1 = outer.float()
    ones_like = torch.ones_like(freqs_1)
    freqs_cis = torch.polar(ones_like, freqs_1)
    
    h = torch.nn.functional.embedding(l_tokens_, l_tok_embeddings_weight_)
    x_normed = h.float()
    pow_2 = x_normed.pow(2)
    mean = pow_2.mean(-1, keepdim=True)
    add = torch.add(mean, 1e-05)
    rsqrt = torch.rsqrt(add)
    x_normed_1 = torch.mul(x_normed, rsqrt)
    type_as = x_normed_1.type_as(h)
    normed_x = torch.mul(type_as, l_attn_norm_0_weight_)
    
    q = torch.nn.functional.linear(normed_x, l_wq_0_weight_)
    k = torch.nn.functional.linear(normed_x, l_wk_0_weight_)
    v = torch.nn.functional.linear(normed_x, l_wv_0_weight_)
    
    view = q.view(2, 4, 8, 8)
    q_1 = view.transpose(1, 2)
    view_1 = k.view(2, 4, 8, 8)
    k_1 = view_1.transpose(1, 2)
    view_2 = v.view(2, 4, 8, 8)
    v_1 = view_2.transpose(1, 2)
    
    float_3 = q_1.float()
    reshape = float_3.reshape(2, 8, 4, -1, 2)
    xq_ = torch.view_as_complex(reshape)
    
    float_4 = k_1.float()
    reshape_1 = float_4.reshape(2, 8, 4, -1, 2)
    xk_ = torch.view_as_complex(reshape_1)
    
    freqs_cis_1 = freqs_cis.reshape(1, 1, 4, -1)
    mul_2 = torch.mul(xq_, freqs_cis_1)
    view_as_real = torch.view_as_real(mul_2)
    xq_out = view_as_real.flatten(3)
    
    mul_3 = torch.mul(xk_, freqs_cis_1)
    view_as_real_1 = torch.view_as_real(mul_3)
    xk_out = view_as_real_1.flatten(3)
    
    q_2 = xq_out.type_as(q_1)
    k_2 = xk_out.type_as(k_1)
    
    mask = torch.full([1, 1, 4, 4], float('-inf'), device='cpu', dtype=torch.float32)
    mask_1 = torch.triu(mask, diagonal=1)
    transpose_3 = k_2.transpose(-2, -1)
    matmul = torch.matmul(q_2, transpose_3)
    
    scores = torch.mul(matmul, 0.35355339059327373)
    scores_1 = torch.add(scores, mask_1)
    attn_weights = torch.nn.functional.softmax(scores_1, dim=-1)
    attn_output = torch.matmul(attn_weights, v_1)
    
    transpose_4 = attn_output.transpose(1, 2)
    contiguous = transpose_4.contiguous()
    attn_output_1 = contiguous.view(2, 4, 64)
    linear_3 = torch.nn.functional.linear(attn_output_1, l_wo_0_weight_)
    
    return (arange, t, mask, h, angles, mask_1, x_normed, pow_1, pow_2, freqs, mean, outer, add, freqs_1, rsqrt, ones_like, x_normed_1, freqs_cis, type_as, freqs_cis_1, normed_x, q, k, v, view, view_1, view_2, q_1, k_1, v_1, float_3, float_4, reshape, reshape_1, xq_, xk_, mul_2, mul_3, view_as_real, view_as_real_1, xq_out, xk_out, q_2, k_2, transpose_3, matmul, scores, scores_1, attn_weights, attn_output, transpose_4, contiguous, attn_output_1, linear_3)


def get_inputs():
    torch.manual_seed(2077)
    return (
        torch.randn([512, 64], dtype=torch.float32) * 0.1,
        torch.zeros([2, 4], dtype=torch.int64),
```

comments.author: claude[bot]
comments.body:
**Claude finished @jansel's task in 27s** —— [View job](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/actions/runs/29137749290)

---
### Answer

Yes. Autotuning benchmarks each candidate and picks the fastest, so on machines where the ATen `bmm` happens to win, the buggy CPP GEMM/BMM path is never codegen'd. To force the non-ATen (CPP) backend, restrict the GEMM backend list so ATen is not a candidate at all:

**Config:**
```python
import torch._inductor.config as config
config.max_autotune = True
config.max_autotune_gemm_backends = "CPP"   # drop ATEN/TRITON so only the CPP template is a choice
```

**Env var equivalent:**
```bash
TORCHINDUCTOR_MAX_AUTOTUNE=1 \
TORCHINDUCTOR_MAX_AUTOTUNE_GEMM_BACKENDS=CPP \
python bug.py
```

The default is `"ATEN,TRITON,CPP"` (see `torch/_inductor/config.py:648-650`). With only `CPP` in the list, autotuning has just the `cpp_CppMicroGemm*` choice, so it is selected regardless of measured timing — which should reproduce the `AssertionError: len(index) == len(stride)` in `ir.py`'s `indexer` deterministically, independent of the CPU/ISA.

Notes:
- On CPU you can drop `TRITON` (no effect), but keeping it in the list is harmless.
- If you additionally want to skip the benchmarking step entirely, `config.autotune_fallback_to_aten = False` combined with the above keeps ATen out of any fallback path too, though it isn't required just to force the CPP choice here.

issues.title: Dynamo graph break in native bmm_outer_product eager router due to _is_cow_tensor / call_boxed
issues.author: armijo1122
issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

Hi PyTorch team, thanks for the work on the new native override path.

We hit a Dynamo graph break in a larger distributed `torch.compile` training workload on recent PyTorch main. The user code is a regular `torch.matmul`, but during tracing it enters the native `bmm_outer_product` eager router and breaks on the COW check:

```python
# torch/_native/ops/bmm_outer_product/triton_impl.py

a_is_cow = torch._C._is_cow_tensor(a)
b_is_cow = torch._C._is_cow_tensor(b)
```

The relevant user code is conceptually:

```python
querys_K = torch.matmul(torch.reshape(querys, [-1, nh, 1, att_emb_size]), K)
```

The workload has tensor/distributed wrappers around the model, so I suspect this path may differ from a tiny direct `torch.compile(torch.bmm)` repro. A direct minimal `torch.compile` script with outer-product-shaped `bmm` did not reproduce for me, but the larger workload consistently reports graph breaks at the native eager router.

### Error/log snippet

With `TORCH_LOGS=graph_breaks TORCHDYNAMO_VERBOSE=1`:

```text
Graph break in user code at torch/_native/ops/bmm_outer_product/triton_impl.py:35
Graph Break Reason: Encountered graph break when attempting to trace CALL
Attempted to call function marked as skipped
Explanation: Dynamo does not know how to trace the builtin `torch._C..._is_cow_tensor.`
Developer debug context: module: torch._C, qualname: ..._is_cow_tensor, skip reason: cannot determine source file for torch._C (likely a C extension or builtin)

Most recent call last:
  torch/_native/registry.py:923 in eager_router
    result = _dispatch(args, kwargs, swallow_cond_exceptions=False)
  torch/_native/registry.py:913 in _dispatch
    matched = cond(*args, **kwargs)
  torch/_native/ops/bmm_outer_product/triton_impl.py:35 in _bmm_outer_product_cond
    a_is_cow = torch._C._is_cow_tensor(a)
```

There is also a related fallback graph break when the eager router reaches the boxed fallback path:

```text
Graph break in user code at torch/_native/registry.py:925
Graph Break Reason: CALL_FUNCTION_EX
Unsupported method call
Explanation: Dynamo does not know how to trace method `call_boxed` of class `_SafeKernelFunction`

  torch/_native/registry.py:925 in eager_router
    return _fallback.call_boxed(keyset, *args, **kwargs)
```

This seems related to the comment in `torch/_native/registry.py` saying that compile/export routers run under FakeTensor, where predicates such as `_is_cow_tensor` may be undefined, so cond exceptions are swallowed and no-match returns `NotImplemented`. In this workload, however, Dynamo still appears to trace through `eager_router`, where `_is_cow_tensor` and `_fallback.call_boxed` are not trace-safe.

### Question

Is this expected behavior for the native `bmm_outer_product` override, or should the eager router avoid running these non-traceable checks while Dynamo is compiling?

Would a reasonable fix be one of the following?

1. Route native overrides through the compile-safe `compile_router` when Dynamo is tracing.
2. Make the eager router return a trace-safe fallback under `torch.compiler.is_compiling()` instead of calling `_fallback.call_boxed`.
3. Avoid querying `_is_cow_tensor` in the compile-time predicate and treat this as a no-match/default lowering case.

A local workaround seems to be disabling the bmm native override before compilation:

```python
import torch._native
from torch._native.registry import deregister_op_overrides

deregister_op_overrides(disable_op_symbols="bmm")
```

But it would be useful to know what the intended fix/design is.

### Versions

Observed on a local main build:

```text
Base PyTorch commit before local changes: ef8a54fb6d161bd81ef349c2adc283589deccb9f
CUDA: 13.1
Python: 3.11
```

Thanks!

cc @chauhang @penguinwu @voznesenskym @EikanWang @jgong5 @Guobing-Chen @XiaobingSuper @zhuhaozhe @blzheng @wenzhe-nrv @jiayisunx @kadeng @amjames @jataylo @azahed98

comments.body:
I was able to reduce this to a small local repro test. One important trigger is that the `matmul` runs under a `torch.device("cuda")` context, which routes the call through `torch.utils._device.DeviceContext.__torch_function__`. That makes Dynamo trace into the native bmm eager router instead of the usual direct compiled bmm path.

This test currently fails because `counters["graph_break"]` contains both `_is_cow_tensor` and `call_boxed` graph breaks. It should pass if the native bmm override avoids tracing the eager router path during compilation.

```python
import unittest

import torch
import torch._dynamo
from torch._dynamo.utils import counters


@unittest.skipIf(not torch.cuda.is_available(), "requires CUDA")
class NativeBmmOuterProductGraphBreakReproTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def tearDown(self):
        counters.clear()
        torch._dynamo.reset()

    def test_device_context_matmul_does_not_trace_native_bmm_eager_router(self):
        counters.clear()

        @torch.compile(dynamic=False)
        def fn(q, k):
            with torch.device("cuda"):
                a = torch.reshape(q, [-1, 8, 1, 32])
                return torch.matmul(a, k)

        q = torch.randn(64, 8 * 32, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float16)
        k = torch.randn(1, 8, 32, 128, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float16)

        out = fn(q, k)
        torch.cuda.synchronize()
        self.assertEqual(out.shape, (64, 8, 1, 128))

        graph_break_reasons = "\n".join(counters["graph_break"].keys())
        self.assertNotIn("_is_cow_tensor", graph_break_reasons)
        self.assertNotIn("call_boxed", graph_break_reasons)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(unittest.main())
```

Current failure on my local build based on upstream commit `ef8a54fb6d161bd81ef349c2adc283589deccb9f`:

```text
AssertionError: '_is_cow_tensor' unexpectedly found in ...
Dynamo does not know how to trace the builtin `torch._C..._is_cow_tensor.`
...
Unsupported method call
Dynamo does not know how to trace method `call_boxed` of class `_SafeKernelFunction`
```

A direct minimal `torch.compile` test that calls `torch.bmm`/`torch.matmul` without the device context did not reproduce this for me, which seems consistent with the issue only appearing when Dynamo traces through `DeviceContext.__torch_function__` into the native eager router.
